rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every essence can receive a word: essences are infinite, and what cannot be distinctly apprehended cannot be assigned a name.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن أن تكون جميع الماهيات مسميات بالألفاظ لأن الماهيات غير متناهية وما لا نهاية له لا يكون مشعورا به على التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more urgent a meaning is to express, the more fitting it is to coin a word for it; commands, prohibitions, generality, and particularity illustrate this need.
rows.anchor: كل معنى كانت الحاجة إلى التعبير عنه أهم كان وضع اللفظ بإزائه أولى مثل صيغ الأوامر والنواهي والعموم والخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common word cannot name a meaning hidden from most people: common الحركة denotes bodily movement, not the obscure cause proposed by some theologians.
rows.anchor: المعنى الذي يكون خفيا عند الجمهور يمتنع كونه مسمى باللفظ المشهور مثاله لفظة الحركة لفظة مشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, الحركة names the transition itself, while knowledge and power name being knowing and being capable, not hidden causes of those states.
rows.anchor: الحركة اسم لنفس هذا الانتقال لا للمعنى الذي يوجب الانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meaning is the mental image intended by a speaker, not external things in themselves; external objects are meant only secondarily.
rows.anchor: المعنى اسم للصورة الذهنية لا للموجودات الخارجية لأن المعنى عبارة عن الشيء الذي عناه العاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference between plant sweetness and sugar-candy sweetness lacks a dedicated word, so it can be described only relationally; a coined term would make verbal definition possible.
rows.anchor: حلاوة النبات وحلاوة الطبرزذ فلما لم توضع لتلك التفرقة لفظة مخصوصة لا جرم لا يمكن تعريفها باللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot name a private inner state for listeners who have never conceived it; if a group first conceived that state and coined a term, they could define it verbally.
rows.anchor: استحال لهذا المدرك وضع لفظ لتعريفه لأن السامع ما لم يعرف المسمى أولا لم يمكنه أن يفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaytan derives from distance, whereas the obedient servant is near; the nearness of God and the command to draw near support this contrast.
rows.anchor: وأما المطيع فقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajim means pelted by the arrows of curse and misery, while the servant is joined to felicity by God's word of piety.
rows.anchor: وأما الرجيم فهو المرجوم بمعنى كونه مرميا بسهم اللعن والشقاوة وأما أنت فموصول بحبل السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God's established way does not change, the nearness He grants the servant means He will not drive that servant from His bounty and mercy.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى أخبر إنه لا يجعل الشيطان الذي هو بعيد قريبا

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says seeking refuge is required before recitation, unlike other acts of obedience, because it cleanses a tongue soiled by lying, backbiting, and gossip.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق : إنه لا بد قبل القراءة من التعوذ وأما سائر الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is framed as an invitation to leave the accursed Satan and reach the All-Merciful, the Compassionate.
rows.anchor: إنه شيطان رجيم وأنا رحمن رحيم فابعد عن الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is an unseen enemy while God is the victorious beloved; when the hidden enemy attacks, the servant should turn to the victorious beloved.
rows.anchor: الشيطان عدوك وأنت عنه غافل غائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises why the command says “I seek refuge in God,” which lacks exclusivity, rather than “By God I seek refuge,” though the latter is stronger; he compares الحمد لله and لله الحمد.
rows.anchor: فرق بين أن يقال أعوذ بالله وبين أن يقال بالله أعوذ فإن الأول لا يفيد الحصر والثاني يفيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A particle is distinguished from noun and verb because its meaning is not independently intelligible; a noun is independently intelligible without indicating a specific time, whereas a verb indicates time.
rows.anchor: الكلمة إما أن يكون معناها مستقلا بالمعلومية أو لا يكون وهذا الأخير هو الحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ضرب indicates that striking issued from something, but does not itself identify that agent.
rows.anchor: ضرب فهو يدل على صدور الضرب عن شيء ما إلا أن ذلك الشيء غير مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that a verb is assigned to an agent the speaker will specify, not to an entity left indefinite in reality; before specification the utterance is incomplete and not truth-apt.
rows.anchor: ضرب صيغة غير موضوعة لإسناد الضرب إلى شيء مبهم في نفس الأمر بل وضعت لإسناده إلى شيء معين يذكره ذلك القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar definition of a particle as one whose meaning occurs in another is ambiguous: one reading would make names of accidents and attributes particles, another is plainly false, and any third needs explanation.
rows.anchor: قالوا الحرف ما جاء المعنى في غيره وهذا لفظ مبهم لأنهم إن أرادوا معنى الحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of the six possible combinations of noun, verb, and particle, noun+noun and noun+verb form informative sentences by agreement; the excerpt begins considering noun+particle forms.
rows.anchor: التركيبات الممكنة من هذه الثلاثة ستة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poetic example treats uttering only the letter qāf as a saying or statement.
rows.anchor: قلت لها قفي فقالت قاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl can stand metaphorically for beliefs and doctrines: saying someone follows Abu Ḥanīfa or Mālik means adopting their beliefs; calling a denial of vision the Muʿtazila’s qawl is apt, while kalām would be strained.
rows.anchor: لفظ القول يصح جعله مجازا عن الاعتقادات والآراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāla may describe nonverbal expression: poets make birds, eyes, and a full water trough “speak,” as do the Qurʾānic commands to creation to say “Be” and to heaven and earth to come.
rows.anchor: لفظ قال قد يستعمل في غير النطق

rows.speaker: الذين ينكرون كلام النفس
rows.claim: Those who deny inner speech hold that kalām and qawl name only spoken words and uttered expressions.
rows.anchor: الذين ينكرون كلام النفس اتفقوا على أن الكلام والقول اسم لهذه الألفاظ والكلمات

rows.speaker: مثبتو كلام النفس
rows.claim: Proponents of inner speech say the inward mental meaning is also called kalām and qawl, citing the Qurʾānic description of the hypocrites as liars.
rows.anchor: أما مثبتو كلام النفس فقد اتفقوا على أن ذلك المعنى النفساني يسمى بالكلام وبالقول واحتجوا عليه بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that proof: the hypocrites lied in claiming to bear witness, since testimony requires knowledge and they lacked it, even though Muhammad is truly God's messenger.
rows.anchor: الشهادة لا تحصل إلا مع العلم وهم ما كانوا عالمين به فثبت أنهم كانوا كاذبين فيما أخبروا عنه بالقول اللساني

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: At the Saqīfa, ʿUmar said he had prepared words inwardly, but Abū Bakr spoke before him.
rows.anchor: ما نقل أن عمر قال يوم السقيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek refuge applies to every creature, not a single person, since God recounts prophets and saints doing so; Razi says all creatures must seek refuge in God.
rows.anchor: أمر منه لعباده أن يقولوا ذلك وهذا غير مختص بشخص معين

words: رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسأل
rows.speaker: نوح
rows.claim: Noah sought refuge from asking God about what he did not know; God then granted him the gifts of peace and blessings.
rows.anchor: حكى عن نوح عليه السلام

words: معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي
rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: When the woman tried to seduce Joseph, he sought God's protection; God granted him protection from evil and indecency.
rows.anchor: حكى عن يوسف عليه السلام أن المرأة لما راودته

words: معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده
rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: When asked to keep one brother in place of Benjamin, Joseph refused to seize anyone except the one with the found property; Razi links his later honor to this refuge in God.
rows.anchor: معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده

words: أعوذ بالله أن أكون من الجاهلين
rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: When his people accused him of mockery over the cow command, Moses sought refuge from ignorance; God removed the accusation and brought the slain man back to life.
rows.anchor: أن القوم لما خوفوه بالقتل

words: إني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون
rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: When threatened with stoning, Moses sought refuge in his and their Lord; God granted his request, destroyed their enemy, and gave them the enemy's land and homes.
rows.anchor: أن القوم لما خوفوه بالقتل

words: وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم
rows.speaker: امرأة عمران
rows.claim: Mary's mother entrusted her and her descendants to God's protection from Satan, and God accepted Mary and caused her to grow well.
rows.anchor: فوجدت الخلعة والقبول وهو قوله

words: إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا
rows.speaker: مريم
rows.claim: When Gabriel appeared to her as a man in seclusion, Mary sought refuge in the Merciful; she received a son without a father and was vindicated by the child's declaration of servitude to God.
rows.anchor: أن مريم عليها السلام لما رأت جبريل في صورة بشر

words: رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين
rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: God repeatedly commanded Muhammad to seek refuge from satanic promptings and their presence, as well as to recite the two refuge sūras.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أمر محمدا عليه الصلاة والسلام بالاستعاذة مرة بعد أخرى

words: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses command answering evil with what is better and seeking refuge when Satan provokes; Razi says they show prophets continually sought protection from evil human and jinn devils.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآيات دالة على أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام كانوا أبدا في الاستعاذة من شر شياطين الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿādh ibn Jabal reports that two men quarreled and traded insults before the Prophet; the excerpt stops as the Prophet begins to answer.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary analysis makes the pronoun in ربه refer to an earlier mention; Ibn Jinnī allows it to refer to ʿAdī, contrary to the majority, but Razi says the argument should be framed differently.
rows.anchor: أن الهاء عائدة إلى مذكور متقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transitive act needs both an agent as influencer and an object as recipient; neither precedes the other in the act itself, so just as the agent may precede, the object may precede in wording.
rows.anchor: الفعل المتعدي لا يستغني عن المفعول وذلك لأن الفاعل هو المؤثر والمفعول هو القابل والفعل مفتقر إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ضرب غلامه زيد the object appears before the subject in wording, although it remains later in meaning.
rows.anchor: وهو كقولك ضرب غلامه زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about Abraham being tested by his Lord, the subject is later in wording but earlier in meaning; making that semantic order explicit would yield an antecedent before its pronoun.
rows.anchor: الإضمار قبل الذكر غير حاصل في الصورة لكنه حاصل في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A subject may be explicit, an overt attached pronoun, or an unexpressed implicit pronoun, as in ضرب زيد, ضربت, ضربنا, and زيد ضرب.
rows.anchor: الفاعل قد يكون مظهرا كقولك : ضرب زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject can be omitted in إذا كان غدا, understood as “what we are on” when tomorrow comes.
rows.anchor: إذا كان ما نحن عليه غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb may also be omitted: replying زيد to “Who did it?” means “Zayd did it”; the verse about a polytheist seeking protection is analyzed with an implied verb before أحد.
rows.anchor: فتقول : زيد والتقدير فعل زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises an objection that pairing Satan the Accursed with the All-Merciful implies parity and resembles dualism, whose adherents treat God and Iblis as two brothers, one good and one evil.
rows.anchor: الشيطان مبالغة في الشيطنة كما أن الرحمن مبالغة في الرحمة والرجيم في حق الشيطان فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God is merciful and generous, the objector asks why He created Satan and empowered him over people; if not, the objector asks why anyone should seek refuge in Him.
rows.anchor: الإله هل هو رحيم كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks whether angels in heaven seek refuge from Satan, and suggests that if they do, they must mean protection from their own evil rather than Satan's.
rows.anchor: فإن ذكروه فإنما يستعيذون من شرور أنفسهم لا من شرور الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also asks whether the people of Paradise say “I seek refuge in God” while already in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أهل الجنة في الجنة هل يقولون أعوذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Why do prophets and the truthful seek refuge when Satan says he has no hold over God's sincere servants?
rows.anchor: مع أن الشيطان أخبر أنه لا تعلق له بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Satan claims only to invite and humans accept, Razi asks why people seek refuge from Satan rather than from their own selves, which they themselves lead into danger.
rows.anchor: الشيطان أخبر أنه لا تعلق له بهم إلا في مجرد الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says this sūra could yield ten thousand useful questions; he added the preface to show that such a number is attainable and not difficult to reach.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة الكريمة يمكن أن يستنبط من فوائدها ونفائسها عشرة آلاف مسألة فاستبعد هذا بعض الحساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited matter, whether a matter of belief or an act of the limbs.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الاستعاذة بالله من جميع المنهيات والمحظورات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report Razi calls well known says the community will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one; he gives no grading beyond calling it famous.
rows.anchor: في الخبر المشهور قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ستفترق أمتي على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة كلهم في النار إلا فرقة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi takes the report to imply that the other seventy-two sects hold false doctrines across many questions: God's essence, attributes, rulings, acts and names, free will, justice, reward, afterlife, promise, status, and imamate.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الاثنتين والسبعين موصوفون بالعقائد الفاسدة والمذاهب الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because refuge from a thing requires knowing what it is and knowing its false or evil character, the formula encompasses ten thousand or more or fewer important issues.
rows.anchor: والاستعاذة من الشيء لا تمكن إلا بعد معرفة المستعاذ منه وإلا بعد معرفة كون ذلك الشيء باطلا وقبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿūdhu derives from ʿawdh, meaning either to seek refuge and protection or to cling; accordingly, the formula means seeking God's mercy and protection or clinging to His grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: مشتق من العوذ وله معنيان : أحدهما : الالتجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation makes Satan come from shatana, “to be distant”; rebels among jinn, humans, and animals are so called for being far from right guidance, as the verse and ʿUmar's anecdote illustrate.
rows.anchor: الأول أنه مشتق من الشطن وهو البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second etymology derives Satan from shāṭa yashīṭu, “to become void”; the rebel is like something void because he nullifies his own interests.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني أن الشيطان مأخوذ من قوله شاط يشيط إذا بطل ولما كان كل متمرد كالباطل في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajim means one pelted and is faʿīl with passive force, like khadib for dyed and laʿin for cursed.
rows.anchor: وأما الرجيم فمعناه المرجوم فهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Satan is rajim because God has cursed him; rajm can mean cursing, as in the command expelling Satan and Abraham's father's threat.
rows.anchor: أن كونه مرجوما كونه ملعونا من قبل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Satan is called rajim because God ordered angels to drive devils from the heavens with meteors; the description then extends to every evil rebel.
rows.anchor: أن الشيطان إنما وصف بكونه مرجوما لأنه تعالى أمر الملائكة برمي الشياطين بالشهب والثواقب طردا لهم من السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Hearing, the Knowing” suits seeking refuge because satanic whispers are hidden; God hears every sound, knows every secret and can repel them.
rows.anchor: الغرض من الاستعاذة الاحتراز من شر الوسوسة ومعلوم أن الوسوسة كأنها حروف خفية في قلب الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation for using “the Hearing, the Knowing” here is simply that this wording follows the Qurʾānic formula in the commands to seek refuge from Satan's prompting.
rows.anchor: إنما تعين هذا الذكر بهذا الموضع اقتداء بلفظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says jinn had accepted Islam in Medina; people should warn one appearing to them for three days and kill it if it returns, since then it is a devil. The excerpt gives no narrator.
rows.anchor: إن بالمدينة جنا قد أسلموا فمن بدا لكم منهم فآذنوه ثلاثة أيام فإن بدا لكم بعد ذلك فاقتلوه

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿīd reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet saw an afrit pursuing him with a flame; Gabriel taught him a supplication that would extinguish it and make the afrit fall face-first.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد : قال

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel taught the Prophet a refuge prayer invoking God's face and perfect words against harms descending from heaven, rising from earth, and arriving by night or day, except a benevolent visitor.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل عليه السلام : ألا أعلمك كلمات

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār is reported in Mālik's Muwaṭṭaʾ as seeking refuge in God's mighty face, complete words, and all His names from everything He created.
rows.anchor: كان يقول : أعوذ بوجه الله العظيم الذي ليس شيء أعظم منه

rows.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
rows.claim: Khālid ibn al-Walīd told the Prophet he was frightened in sleep; the Prophet taught him to seek refuge in God's complete words from divine anger, punishment, creatures' evil, satanic promptings, and their presence.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله إني أروع في منامي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Razi says the Prophet's nighttime visit to the jinn, recitation to them, and invitation to Islam is widely known and has reached mass-transmitted status.
rows.anchor: ما اشتهر وبلغ مبلغ التواتر من خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن وقراءته عليهم ودعوته إياهم إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
rows.claim: A report cited by al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says Jesus asked God to show Satan's place in a human; Satan appeared serpent-headed over the heart, withdrawing when God is remembered and resting on the heart when not.
rows.anchor: روى القاضي أبو بكر في الهداية أن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام دعا ربه أن يريه موضع الشيطان من بني آدم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan runs through the human being like blood.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان ليجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report says everyone has a satan; a questioner asks whether this includes the Prophet, but the excerpt ends before the Prophet's answer.
rows.anchor: ما منكم أحد إلا وله شيطان
